title: Socket supervision presets and timeout heuristics for SDKs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: SDK consumers struggle to pick robust transport defaults that balance latency, connection churn, and resource usage across hosting environments (serverless, long‑running backend, desktop). Current per‑language guides are fragmentary and lead to misconfigured clients with excessive reconnects, head‑of‑line blocking during streaming, or resource exhaustion under bursty workloads.

Goal: Provide a cross‑SDK 'socket supervision' spec with opinionated presets and heuristics for: connection keepalive, connection pool sizing, per‑request and per‑stream timeouts, idle pruning, backoff for retries, and examples demonstrating best practices in Python, TypeScript, and Go. Deliverables: canonical defaults, detailed config knobs, sample code snippets, e2e telemetry hooks, and a migration note for existing users.

Constraints: keep API ergonomics consistent across SDKs; avoid adding new heavyweight abstractions; preserve streaming ergonomics (low latency for first bytes and stable throughput for long responses).
acceptance_criteria: A cross‑SDK spec doc checked into repo that defines default values for: dial/connect timeout, request timeout, streaming frame idle timeout, TCP keepalive, maximum pooled connections per host, and idle connection pruning interval.
Reference implementations/patches in Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs that wire the defaults and expose opt‑out knobs with clear names.
Integration tests that simulate bursty traffic and verify that the pool does not exceed configured limits and that idle connections are pruned within expected windows.
Telemetry events emitted for pool size changes, connection open/close reasons, and retransmissions/retries to allow post‑deploy analysis.
Guides and code examples added to developer docs for three common deployment profiles: serverless, microservice, and desktop client.
Performance guideline table showing tradeoffs (latency vs. resource usage) for each profile.
implementation_notes: Use a single canonical name for knobs across SDKs: e.g., connection.dial_timeout_ms, connection.request_timeout_ms, connection.keepalive_interval_ms, connection.max_pool_per_host, connection.idle_prune_ms, streaming.frame_idle_timeout_ms.
Prefer millisecond integers for cross‑language parity; provide helpers to convert human durations in each SDK where idiomatic (e.g., Python timedelta, TS number | string, Go time.Duration).

For streaming, decouple request timeout (overall RPC) from frame idle timeout to avoid cancelling long but active streams. Default: request_timeout_ms=0 (disabled) and frame_idle_timeout_ms=60_000 for long polls; provide profile presets that set request_timeout_ms for short RPCs.

Backoff policy: default retry backoff with jitter, with a short circuit for idempotent unary calls only. Streaming reconnects use exponential backoff capped at 30s, and immediate reconnect attempts are limited to 2 tries to avoid thundering herd.
Pool sizing heuristics: default max_pool_per_host = min(50, cpu_count * 4) for long‑running backends; for serverless preset reduce to 4 to avoid socket exhaustion from ephemeral invocations.

Telemetry: emit structured event tags: sdk_lang, profile, pool_size_after_op, connection_open_reason, connection_close_reason, retry_count, last_backoff_ms. Keep events low cardinality and sample at 1% by default for non‑error flows.
For TLS/H2 multiplexing: document that HTTP/2 multiplexing changes pooling semantics; when multiplexing is available, recommend lowering max_pool_per_host and increasing concurrency per connection.
Edge cases: describe behavior when underlying OS limits file descriptors: SDKs should surface a clear warning log and metric 'fd_limit_reached' and provide a config to fail fast.
progress_updates: 2025-02-18: Initial RFC written and synced with SDK leads (Python, TS, Go). Collected examples of problematic configs from support tickets and customer feedback.
2025-02-20: Consensus on canonical knob names reached in cross‑sdk sync. Agreed to use ms integers and standardized telemetry tag names.
2025-02-22: Python PR opened that adds connection pool glue and exposes 'profiles' object (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/412). Unit tests for pool sizing added.

2025-02-24: TS prototype implemented using fetch + keepalive agent with examples for serverless and desktop (PR draft: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/298). Need review on ergonomics for web vs node.
2025-02-25: Go implementation WIP. Experiment showed that streaming frame idle timeout must be separate from unary RPC timeout to avoid premature cancellations.
2025-02-26: Telemetry schema draft posted to infra telemetry board (link below). Requested retention and sampling guidance from observability team.
review_feedback: Design: keep the public surface minimal; prefer simple 'profile' presets with opt‑out granular knobs. (Lena Fisher)
Security: ensure that keepalive and idle pruning do not disable TLS renegotiation windows; no secrets are stored in config. (Rahul Mehta)
SRE: prefer conservative defaults for serverless to avoid socket exhaustion; suggested adding a diagnostic mode exposing per‑process connection counts. (Jules Caron)
PM: Add short migration notes for customers upgrading from older SDKs that had different defaults. (Morgan Lee)
next_steps: Finish Go PR and run cross‑sdk e2e scenarios in staging cluster simulating 10k concurrent short unary requests and 200 long streams.
Wire telemetry into central pipeline and validate low‑cardinality tags in staging dashboards.
Write migration doc and three example recipes for serverless, microservice, and desktop in docs repo.
Schedule demo with Developer Relations to review examples and get feedback on ergonomic surface.
